ai.description: The Bhamo frog reaches 5–6 cm. It is brown with a distinct dark, triangular patch covering the tympanum and a pale, cream-colored dorsolateral fold. A white stripe typically borders the upper lip.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Humerana humeralis* is best distinguished by the prominent, enlarged, and glandular humeral gland located on the upper arm, which is absent in similar Indian ranids.
ai.habitat: The Bhamo Frog inhabits moist, subtropical evergreen forests and bamboo thickets in the Indian subcontinent, typically found near streams at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Bhamo frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates along the edges of streams and forest pools.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Humerana humeralis* is an egg-laying species that breeds during the monsoon season, depositing small clutches of eggs in stagnant or slow-moving water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Bhamo Frog is found in Northeast India, specifically in Arunachal Pradesh and Assam, inhabiting tropical forests at elevations up to 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Bhamo Frog produces a rapid, high-pitched series of "chirp-chirp" notes, typically heard emanating from flooded rice paddies and grassy wetlands.
